Danish

Etymology

From Old Danish huilk, huilkin, from Old Norse hvilíkr, hvílíkr, from Proto-Germanic *hwilīkaz (“what kind of, what sort of”), cognate with English which, German welcher, Gothic 𐍈𐌹𐌻𐌴𐌹𐌺𐍃 (ƕileiks). A compound of *hwaz (“who”) +‎ *-līkaz (“shaped”).

Pronunciation

  • IPA(key): /ˈvelɡən/, [ˈʋe̝lɡ̊ŋ̍]

Pronoun

hvilken (neuter hvilket, plural hvilke)

  1. (interrogative) what, which, the
    Synonym: hvad for
  2. (relative) who, whom, which
    Synonyms: der, som
  3. (fused relative) whatever, whichever (with the particle end)

References

  • “hvilken” in Den Danske Ordbog
  • “hvilken” in Ordbog over det danske Sprog

Norwegian Bokmål

Etymology

PIE word
*kʷís

Inherited from Old Norse hvílíkr (“of what kind”), from Proto-Germanic *hwilīkaz (“of what kind”). The Germanic formation combines the interrogative stem Proto-Germanic *hwi-, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷi-, with Proto-Germanic *-līkaz (“-like”), related to *līką (“body; form”); the further origin of the second element is uncertain.[1] The relative use was influenced by German welcher.[2], and the modern form probably has influence from Danish hvilken.[3]

Cognate with Icelandic hvílíkur and Faroese hvílíkur (“what kind of”), Swedish vilken, Dutch welk, German welcher, Gothic 𐍈𐌹𐌻𐌴𐌹𐌺𐍃 (ƕileiks) and English which.

Pronunciation

  • IPA(key): /¹ʋɪlkən/, [ˈʋɪ̀lkən], [ˈʋɪ̀lkn̩]
  • Rhymes: -ɪlkən
  • Hyphenation: hvil‧ken

Determiner

hvilken (neuter singular hvilket, plural hvilke)

  1. which; asks for a selection from a particular set, in a direct or indirect question
    Hvilken bok skal jeg velge? ― Which book should I choose?
    Jeg vet ikke hvilket tog hun tar. ― I do not know which train she is taking.
    • 1885, Henrik Ibsen, Brand‎, 10th edition, page 126:
      Brand: «Hvilken vej?» (peger først mod havegrinden, siden mod husdøren)
      Brand: “Which way?” (points first towards the garden gate, then towards the door of the house)
    • (rare, before a substantivized adjective)
      1886, Henrik Ibsen, Rosmersholm‎, page 172:
      Rebekka: «Jeg har det store igen.», – Rosmer: «Hvilket store?»
      Rebekka: “I still have the big thing left to tell.” – Rosmer: “What big thing?”
    • 1892, Henrik Ibsen, Bygmester Solness‎, page 203:
      han? Hvilken han?
      he? Which he?
    • 1896, Henrik Ibsen, John Gabriel Borkman‎, page 236:
      riget, siger du? Hvilket rige –?
      the kingdom, you say? Which kingdom –?
    • 2001, Finn Carling, Øynene i parken‎:
      Julietta tenkte, gud vet for hvilken gang, på den siste kvelden før han forsvant
      Julietta thought, for the umpteenth time, about the last evening before he disappeared
  2. what; asks about kind, quality, extent or significance, in a direct or indirect question
    Hvilken betydning har dette for oss? ― What significance does this have for us?
    Jeg forstår ikke hvilken betydning dette har. ― I do not understand what significance this has.
    • 1874, Henrik Ibsen, De unges forbund‎, page 118:
      ved hvilke midler er De kommen ivejret?
      by what means have you risen in the world?
    • 1874, Henrik Ibsen, Fru Inger til Østråt‎, page 100:
      Gud må vide, med hvilken ret jeg bærer det [navnet]
      God knows by what right I bear it [the name]
    • 1879, Henrik Ibsen, Et dukkehjem‎, page 58:
      da får min mand rigtig se, hvilket slet menneske De er
      then my husband will really see what a wicked person you are
    • 1882, Henrik Ibsen, En folkefiende‎, page 74:
      jeg har gjort dig opmærksom på, hvilke interesser der står på spil
      I have made you aware of what interests are at stake
    • 1931, Morgenbladet, number 273, page 1, columns 3–5:
      hvilken tillit kan man ha til de menneskelige utsagn?
      what confidence can one place in people's statements?
    • 1998, Stig Sæterbakken, Selvbeherskelse‎, page 19:
      hvilken makt hadde han over meg, når det kom til stykket?
      what power did he have over me, when it came down to it?
    • 1998, Stig Sæterbakken, Selvbeherskelse‎, page 22:
      har du i det hele tatt noen forestilling om hvilke krav som stilles?
      do you have any idea at all what demands are being made?
    1. what; used rhetorically to imply that none meets the description
      Hvilket menneske ville gjort noe slikt? ― What person would have done such a thing?
      • 1877, Henrik Ibsen, Samfundets støtter‎, page 28:
        hvilke forældre vilde vel betro sine børn til en sådan en?
        what parents would entrust their children to someone like that?
      • 2006, Torbjørn Færøvik, Buddhas barn:
        hvilken bukt i verden kan måle seg med Halong?
        what bay in the world can compare with Ha Long Bay?
  3. what (a); expresses admiration, disapproval, surprise or another emphatic evaluation, in a complete clause or an abbreviated exclamation
    Hvilken fantastisk utsikt! ― What a fantastic view!
    Du aner ikke hvilken fantastisk tur det var. ― You have no idea what a fantastic trip it was.
    • 1873, Henrik Ibsen, Kærlighedens komedie‎, page 22:
      og du er her? Hvilket under!
      and you are here? What a miracle!
    • 1874, Henrik Ibsen, De unges forbund‎, page 71:
      kammerherren, – hvilken prægtig, fin gammel gubbe!
      the chamberlain, – what a splendid, refined old fellow!
    • 1881, Henrik Ibsen, Gengangere‎, page 163:
      ser du, Osvald, hvilken dejlig dag vi får?
      do you see, Osvald, what a lovely day we are going to have?
    • (now rare, with interrogative word order)
      1882, Alexander L. Kielland, Skipper Worse‎, page 53:
      hvilke muntre bordtaler kunde han ikke holde
      what lively dinner speeches he could give!
    • 1900, Vilhelm Krag, Isaac Seehuusen‎, page 56:
      ei, ei, lille jomfru, hvilken yndig kaabe vi dog har paa i aften
      well, well, young lady, what a lovely cloak we are wearing this evening
    • 1992, Dag Solstad, Ellevte roman, bok atten‎, page 41:
      de betrodde Bjørn Hansen hvilken henrivende kvinne Turid Lammers var
      they confided to Bjørn Hansen what a delightful woman Turid Lammers was
    • 1998, Stig Sæterbakken, Selvbeherskelse‎, page 23:
      han fortalte meg hvilket usselt menneske han syntes jeg var
      he told me what a wretched person he thought I was
    • 1998, Stig Sæterbakken, Selvbeherskelse‎, page 20:
      lurendreieri parret med feighet, hvilken edel kombinasjon!
      deceit coupled with cowardice, what a noble combination!
    • 1998, Finn Skårderud, Uro‎, page 265:
      på veien ble jeg fortapt i en Armani-jakke. Hvilken skjønnhetsåpenbaring!
      on the way I fell hopelessly in love with an Armani jacket. What a vision of beauty!
    • 2003, Kirsti Blom, Kitten‎:
      hvilken deilig søndag dette var!
      what a lovely Sunday this was!
  4. whichever, whatever; regardless of which
    Hvilken vei du enn velger, kommer du til sjøen. ― Whichever road you choose, you will reach the sea.
    bildet ville han ha, hvilken pris han så skulle betale ― he wanted the picture, whatever price he might have to pay
    In the expression hvilken som helst: “any; whichever”. Du kan velge hvilken som helst bok. ― You can choose any book.
    • 1875, Henrik Ibsen, Catilina‎, page 67:
      lad dem bringe hvilket bud de vil!
      let them bring whatever message they like!
    • 2009, Simen Hagerup, Grufulle tomrom:
      hvilket tema hun enn velger, tar digresjonene straks over
      whatever topic she chooses, the digressions immediately take over
  5. (obsolete) which; introduces a noun restating something previously mentioned
    Han ba om mer tid, hvilket ønske ble innvilget. ― He asked for more time, which request was granted.
    • 1895, Elias Kræmmer, Glade Borgere‎, volume II, page 72:
      [han] bad om en halv øl, hvilket ønske hans kampfæller ikke fandt at kunne imødekomme
      [he] asked for half a beer, which request his comrades did not feel able to grant

Pronoun

hvilken (neuter singular hvilket, plural hvilke)

  1. which (one or ones); asks for a selection without a following noun, in a direct or indirect question
    Jeg har to nøkler. Hvilken passer? ― I have two keys. Which one fits?
    Hvilke vil du ha? ― Which ones do you want?
    • 1872, Henrik Ibsen, Kongs-Emnerne‎, page 94:
      bisp Nikolas: «Giv mig så papirerne –» – Sira Viljam (går til skrivebordet): «Hvilke, herre?»
      Bishop Nikolas: “Then give me the papers –” – Sira Viljam (goes to the writing desk): “Which ones, my lord?”
    • 1888, Henrik Ibsen, Fruen fra havet‎, page 103:
      jeg ved ikke, hvilken af delene det er
      I do not know which of the alternatives it is
    • 1988, Lars Saabye Christensen, Herman:
      hvilken av historiene mine liker du best?
      which of my stories do you like best?
    • 1997, Gunnar Staalesen, 1900 Morgenrød‎:
      de [ble] stående og diskutere hvilken av filmene de skulle gå på
      they [remained] standing there discussing which of the films they should go and see
    • 2005, Steinar Lem, Det lille livet‎:
      uten å reise meg fra skrivebordet kan jeg plukke en CD, jeg bestemmer selv hvilken
      without getting up from my desk I can pick a CD; I decide for myself which one
    1. (literary) what; asks about the nature of the subject, agreeing with it in gender and number
      Hvilke er dine hensikter? ― What are your intentions?
      • 1875, Henrik Ibsen, Catilina‎, page 73:
        hvilket er dit formål da igrunden?
        what, then, is your purpose, really?
      • 1879, Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson, Det ny system‎, page 128:
        hvilken blir rigsdagens beslutning, tror De?
        what will parliament's decision be, do you think?
    2. (rare) which of two preceding alternatives; specifically the neuter form hvilket, irrespective of their grammatical gender
      Det var en kirke eller en borg; jeg kunne ikke se hvilket. ― It was a church or a castle; I could not tell which.
      • 1903, Otto Sverdrup, Nyt Land‎, volume II, page 356:
        der ligger en ø eller halvø, hvilket kunde vi paa grund af den tætte taage ikke med bestemthed afgjøre
        there lies an island or a peninsula; which it was, we could not determine with certainty owing to the dense fog
  2. (literary) which, who, whom; introduces a relative clause that identifies or supplies additional information about an antecedent
    Vi passerte en bro, under hvilken elva rant. ― We passed a bridge, under which the river flowed.
    • 1883, Henrik Ibsen, “Fortale til anden udgave”, in Gildet på Solhaug‎, 2nd edition, page XIV:
      [gildet] blev den baggrund, imod hvilken handlingen hævede sig frem
      [the feast] became the background against which the action stood out
    • 1903, Otto Sverdrup, Nyt Land‎, volume II, page 41:
      indenfor os havde vi en stor sandør, bag hvilken landet hævede sig svagt
      on the landward side of us was a large sandbank, behind which the land rose gently
    • 1909, Henrik Ibsen, Efterladte Skrifter‎, volume I, page 236:
      [man tar] den første den bedste [boken], hvilken man da … forsømmer at tilbagelevere
      [one takes] the first [book] that comes to hand, which one then … neglects to return
    1. which; specifically hvilket, referring to a whole preceding statement
      Hun kom tidlig, hvilket overrasket meg. ― She arrived early, which surprised me.
      • 1931, Adresseavisen, number 175, page 2, column 1:
        folkene på gården ilte mot fjøsbygningen for å få berget ut besetningen, hvilket også lyktes
        the people on the farm rushed towards the cowshed to rescue the livestock, which they also succeeded in doing
      • 1967, Sigurd Evensmo, Det store tivoli‎, page 291:
        vi er tunge på labben i dette landet … hvilket på film resulterte i anstrengt kavende farse
        we are heavy-handed in this country … which on film resulted in strained, floundering farce
      • 1998, Stig Sæterbakken, Selvbeherskelse‎, page 10:
        jeg ba en stille bønn om at hun ville la emnet ligge, hvilket det også virket som hun ville
        I said a silent prayer that she would drop the subject, which it also seemed she intended to do
      • 2024, Thomas Hylland Eriksen, Det umistelige, page 114:
        for å komme i nærheten av de stedegne artene måtte han enten dykke (hvilket han gjorde alene) eller besøke det lille naturreservatet sørvest på øya (hvilket vi gjorde sammen)
        to get close to the native species, he had to either dive (which he did alone) or visit the small nature reserve in the southwest of the island (which we did together)
    2. (obsolete) which; specifically hvilket, referring to preceding nouns irrespective of gender or number
      Han fant en hatt og en frakk, hvilket han tok med seg. ― He found a hat and a coat, which he took with him.
      • 1879, Henrik Ibsen, Et dukkehjem‎, page 7:
        [bybudet] bærer en julegran og en kurv, hvilket han gier til stuepigen
        [the porter] carries a Christmas tree and a basket, which he gives to the maid
  3. whichever, whatever; any one or ones, regardless of identity
    Hvilken du enn velger, blir jeg fornøyd. ― Whichever you choose, I will be pleased.
    • 1872, Henrik Ibsen, Kongs-Emnerne‎, page 159:
      lad så din sag være hvilken den vil, – jeg ved dog, at jeg strider for det rette!
      let your cause be whatever it may, – I know nevertheless that I fight for what is right!
    • 1874, Henrik Ibsen, Fru Inger til Østråt‎, page 146:
      [dere vil] fremme eders egne anslag, hvilke de end monne være
      [you will] further your own schemes, whatever they may be
  4. (obsolete) what?; specifically hvilket, asking for repetition or clarification
    «Hun hadde visst dratt.» – «Hvilket?» ― “Apparently she had left.” – “What?”
    • 1881, Henrik Ibsen, Gengangere‎, page 44:
      pastor Manders: «Aha, der har vi det altså!» – Fru Alving: «Hvilket?»
      Pastor Manders: “Aha, there we have it, then!” – Mrs Alving: “What?”
    • 1886, Henrik Ibsen, Rosmersholm‎, page 54:
      Kroll: «Tilgiv mig.» – Rosmer: «Hvad? Hvilket?»
      Kroll: “Forgive me.” – Rosmer: “What? What do you mean?”
    • 1898, Kristian Elster, “Tora Trondal”, in Samlede Skrifter‎, volume II, page 14:
      «[Jeg har oppdaget] et Mamuthdyr.» – «Et hvilket?»
      “[I have discovered] a mammoth.” – “A what?”
  5. (dialectal) in the expression hvilket som er: “anyway; in any case”
    Hun kommer ikke, hvilket som er. ― She is not coming, anyway.
    • 1915, Dikken Zwilgmeyer, Inger-Johanne-bøkerne‎, volume IV, page 41:
      frua kjender ikke forskjel på dem, hvilket som er
      the mistress cannot tell the difference between them, in any case

Usage notes

  • Hvilken is used with masculine and feminine singular nouns, hvilket with neuter singular nouns, and hvilke with plural nouns.[4]
  • In indirect questions, som follows the question phrase when that phrase is the subject: Jeg vet ikke hvilken bok som passer (“I do not know which book is suitable”), but Jeg vet ikke hvilken bok du valgte (“I do not know which book you chose”).[5]
  • Relative hvilken is chiefly literary; som is generally used in ordinary language. The neuter hvilket can refer to a whole preceding statement.[2]
  • The dialectal expression hvilket som er arose through reinterpretation of åkkesom.[2]

  • hvem (“who; whom”)
  • hvi (“why”) (archaic or poetic)
  • hvis (“whose”)
  • hvo (“who”) (archaic)
  • hvor (“where; how”)
  • hvordan (“how”)
  • hvorfor (“why”)
  • hvorfra (“from where; whence”) (formal or literary)
  • hvorledes (“how; in what manner”) (literary)
  • hvornår (“when”) (rare, literary)
  • hvortil (“to what; to where”) (literary or dated)
  • hvorvidt (“whether”)
  • når (“when”)
